---
title: "Production deployment"
description: "How omicsbase.utu.fi is laid out, how its images are built and rolled out, and how to roll back."
---

This page is for maintainers of omicsbase.utu.fi. It describes the layout and the usual procedures. It names no addresses, accounts or keys; keep those in a private place.

## Hosts {#hosts}

| Host | What it serves |
| --- | --- |
| `omicsbase.utu.fi` | The notes app (LibreChat). Also `/omics-engine/…` (notes engine files), `/docs/` (these docs), and `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. |
| `openhands.omicsbase.utu.fi` | Reports. It carries the tunnels from Reports sessions, the router's open and close links, and each user's requests to their own session. Without a Reports session it answers `404`. |
| `admin.omicsbase.utu.fi` | The LibreChat admin panel. |

Caddy serves all three with HTTPS, using HARICA certificates. Users sign in with Google or with SAML through the Haka federation (University of Turku included) and eduGAIN. New SAML accounts from `utu.fi` get the `UTU` role and all others the `USER` role, which Google accounts also get. Each role's model list and settings are stored in MongoDB (`configs` collection) and override `librechat.yaml`. LibreChat verifies the Haka and eduGAIN metadata in a child process every 6 hours and caches the result under `data/saml-federation`.

## What runs where {#layout}

**The VM** is a CSC cPouta virtual machine. The checkout lives in `/srv/omicsbase/omicsbase`.

- Docker Compose runs the project `librechat`: LibreChat (`api`), MongoDB, Meilisearch, the file-search services (`vectordb`, `rag_api`), the admin panel and the fallback notes engine.
- Outside Compose, the VM runs:
  - Caddy, the web server (a systemd service).
  - `roihu-router`, the router for Reports sessions (a systemd service).
  - `roihu-relay`, the chisel server that Reports sessions tunnel to (a systemd service).
  - A nightly cron job that rebuilds the sitemap.

**LUMI-K** runs the notes engine as a gateway, shared worker pods that host many notes' R sessions, and pods of their own for heavy notes. The manifest is `deployment/lumi-k/engine.yaml`; its comments explain the sizes.

**Roihu** runs each user's Reports job, in that user's CSC project.

For how requests flow between these, see [How OmicsBase fits together](architecture.qmd).

## Configuration files {#config}

| On the VM | Comes from | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `librechat/.env` | `.env.example` | Secrets, image tags, hosts, Roihu settings. Not in Git. |
| `librechat/librechat.yaml` | `deployment/librechat.yaml` | Model endpoints, the `notethreads` server, model specs. |
| `librechat/docker-compose.override.yml` | `deployment/docker-compose.override.yml` | The production additions to LibreChat's Compose file. |
| `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` | `deployment/Caddyfile.production` | The web server rules. |

The files on the VM are copies. The live Caddyfile has the real host names and certificate settings, so it is kept in step with `deployment/Caddyfile.production` by hand. When you change a rule, change both.

### Settings in `librechat/.env` {#env}

The hosts the browser sees:

```text
DOMAIN_CLIENT=https://omicsbase.example.org
OMICSBASE_APP_HOST=omicsbase.example.org
OMICSBASE_OPENHANDS_PUBLIC_URL=https://openhands.omicsbase.example.org
OMICSBASE_WORKSPACE_HOST=openhands.omicsbase.example.org
OMICSBASE_ENGINE_PUBLIC_URL=https://omicsbase.example.org/omics-engine
OMICSBASE_ADMIN_HOST=admin.omicsbase.example.org
```

The secrets and links between the parts:

| Setting | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `OMICSBASE_AUTH_SECRET` | Shared by LibreChat and Reports. Generate it on its own, never reuse a LibreChat JWT secret. |
| `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET` | Shared by LibreChat and the notes engine. It must equal the engine's secret on LUMI-K. |
| `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_URL` | Where LibreChat sends note cells. Empty means the VM's own engine. |
| `ROIHU_ROUTER_SECRET` | The router's admin secret, which the router keeps in its state folder. |
| `ROIHU_RELAY_FINGERPRINT` | The relay's TLS fingerprint. The relay prints it when it starts. |
| `ROIHU_IMAGE_TAG` | The Reports image that Roihu jobs and own computers use. |
| `OMICSBASE_LIBRECHAT_IMAGE` | The LibreChat image to run. |

To generate a secret:

```bash
openssl rand -hex 32
```

## Run Compose on the VM {#compose}

All Compose commands run from the checkout, with the same files. For example, to recreate LibreChat:

```bash
cd /srv/omicsbase/omicsbase
docker compose --project-directory "$PWD/librechat" --env-file librechat/.env -p librechat \
  -f librechat/docker-compose.yml -f librechat/docker-compose.override.yml \
  up -d --no-deps --force-recreate api
```

## Deploy a new LibreChat image {#librechat}

The LibreChat image is built on the VM. Several server files are not taken from the image: the override mounts them from the checkout in `librechat/` (see the `volumes` of `api` in `docker-compose.override.yml`). The image and the checkout must therefore be at the same fork commit.

1. Note the current image tag (`OMICSBASE_LIBRECHAT_IMAGE` in `librechat/.env`) and the current commit of the `librechat/` checkout. You need both to roll back.
2. Export the new fork commit into a separate build folder, so the live checkout is never half-switched:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p <build folder>
   git -C librechat archive <commit> | tar -x -C <build folder>
   ```

3. Start the build under systemd, so it keeps running if your SSH connection drops:

   ```bash
   sudo systemd-run --unit=build-librechat --working-directory=<build folder> sh -c \
     'docker build --progress=plain --build-arg BUILD_COMMIT=<commit> -t omicsbase-librechat:<short commit> . > build.log 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> build.log'
   ```

4. Check whether it is still running:

   ```bash
   systemctl is-active build-librechat
   ```

   It prints `active` while it runs. A LibreChat build takes about 40 minutes.

5. When it has stopped, read the end of the log:

   ```bash
   tail -n 3 <build folder>/build.log
   ```

   The last line must be `EXIT=0`.

6. Move the `librechat/` checkout to the same commit.
7. Set `OMICSBASE_LIBRECHAT_IMAGE=omicsbase-librechat:<short commit>` in `librechat/.env`.
8. Recreate `api` with `--force-recreate`, as in [Run Compose on the VM](#compose). A plain restart is not enough: a mounted single file keeps pointing at the old file until the container is recreated.
9. Check the server log for the line that lists the `notethreads` tools:

   ```bash
   docker logs LibreChat 2>&1 | grep "Tools:"
   ```

   It must list the tools, such as `execute_r_cell`. If it is missing, notes have no tools.

10. In the browser, run an R cell in a note and open Reports.

Do not run `git pull` on the VM checkout as a deployment step. Move it to an exact commit.

## Notes engine on LUMI-K {#engine}

The LUMI-K image must run as a random non-root user. It is the released engine image with `deployment/rahti/Dockerfile` on top. The plain engine image fails there.

1. Make the release, so that CI has pushed `ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-engine:<version>` ([Make a release](contributing.qmd#release)).
2. On the VM, sign in to LUMI-K with `oc login`, then sign root's Docker in to the LUMI-K registry:

   ```bash
   sudo docker login -u "$(oc whoami)" -p "$(oc whoami -t)" registry.apps.v1.lumi-k.eu
   ```

3. Build, test and push the LUMI-K image from the VM checkout:

   ```bash
   sudo scripts/push_engine_lumik.sh <version>
   ```

   It pulls the release, adds the LUMI-K layer, starts it as a random user in group 0, pushes it and prints its name, `registry.apps.v1.lumi-k.eu/omicsbase-utu/omicsbase-engine:lumik-<version>`.

4. Switch the engine to it and wait for the rollout:

   ```bash
   oc set image deploy/omicsbase-engine engine=<printed name>
   oc rollout status deploy/omicsbase-engine --timeout=15m
   ```

5. Delete the note workers. The gateway starts new ones from its own image:

   ```bash
   oc delete pod -l omicsbase-worker=true
   ```

   Open notes restart their R session once and restore their saved objects.

To roll back, set the previous image in step 4 and delete the workers again.

The engine's secret on LUMI-K is a Kubernetes secret, created separately (see the header of `engine.yaml`). If you change `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_SECRET`, change it on both sides.

### Switch notes between LUMI-K and the VM {#engine-switch}

Three settings decide where notes run:

1. `OMICSBASE_ENGINE_URL` in `librechat/.env`.
2. The `url` of `notethreads` in `librechat/librechat.yaml` (the VM engine is `http://engine:8001/sse`).
3. The `@engine_runs` rule in the Caddyfile, which sends plot requests to LUMI-K.

Change all three together, then recreate `api` and reload Caddy:

```bash
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

## Reports on Roihu {#roihu}

The router and the relay run as systemd services on the VM. The router keeps its routes, relay credentials and secrets in `/srv/omicsbase/roihu-relay`.

### Update the router {#roihu-router}

1. Copy the current file to a backup next to it.
2. Copy the new `deployment/roihu/roihu_router.py` into place.
3. Restart the service:

   ```bash
   sudo systemctl restart roihu-router
   ```

### Roll out a new Reports image {#roihu-image}

1. From the repository root, build the Reports image. This also builds the interface into `openhands/build/`, which the next step copies:

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/build_openhands.py --context default
   ```

2. Build the Roihu image on top of it:

   ```bash
   docker build -f deployment/roihu/Dockerfile --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=omicsbase-openhands:dev \
     -t ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-reports:<tag> .
   ```

   Tags follow the pattern `v<OpenHands version>-roihu<n>`, for example `v1.41.0-roihu4`.

3. Push it:

   ```bash
   docker push ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-reports:<tag>
   ```

4. On Roihu, submit the Slurm job `deployment/roihu/pull_image.sbatch` with `REPORTS_TAG=<tag>` and `REPORTS_IMAGES=<folder>` set. It turns the image into an Apptainer file, `omicsbase-reports_<tag>.sif`.
5. On a Roihu login node, publish that file:

   ```bash
   deployment/roihu/publish_sif.sh <path to .sif> <tag>
   ```

   It asks for a GitHub user and a token with `write:packages`, and ends with `Published oras://ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-reports:<tag>-sif`. Each project's first launch then downloads this one file and skips the conversion.

6. Set `ROIHU_IMAGE_TAG=<tag>` in `librechat/.env` and recreate `api`.

Each CSC project gets the new image on its first launch after the change. The old image files stay in the projects' `images/` folders.

## Search engines {#seo}

- `robots.txt` and the search-console verification file come from `deployment/seo/`. They are copied to `/srv/omicsbase/seo`, where Caddy serves them.
- `sitemap.xml` lists the front page and every public note. `scripts/build_sitemap.sh` writes it to `/srv/omicsbase/seo/sitemap.xml` every night at 03:15 UTC, from cron.
- To list new public notes the same day, run the script by hand on the VM. It ends with `<n> examples written to /srv/omicsbase/seo/sitemap.xml`.
- `robots.txt` also points to the docs' own sitemap.

## Publish the docs {#docs}

Caddy serves `/docs/` from `/srv/omicsbase/docs`. `scripts/publish_docs.sh` fills that folder.

You need Quarto 1.11 or later, `gh`, `rsync`, and SSH access to the VM.

1. From the repository root, publish the current docs:

   ```bash
   OMICSBASE_VM=<user>@<host> scripts/publish_docs.sh
   ```

   It ends with:

   ```text
   Published: https://omicsbase.utu.fi/docs/
   ```

2. For a release, add the version. The script also keeps a copy at `/docs/<version>/`:

   ```bash
   OMICSBASE_VM=<user>@<host> scripts/publish_docs.sh <version>
   ```

Set `OMICSBASE_SSH_KEY` to choose a key file. The script rebuilds the changelog, renders with the `publish` profile and stops if `llms.txt` is missing. It replaces the top level of `/docs/` and keeps the release copies. The release copies have no `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` or `llms.txt`, so the docs sitemap lists only the current docs.

## Roll back {#rollback}

Prepare the way back before every change:

- Before you edit a file on the VM, copy it next to itself with a dated suffix, for example `Caddyfile.bak-<yyyymmdd>-<what>`.
- Keep the previous image. Note its tag and the matching checkout commit.

To go back:

| What changed | How to undo it |
| --- | --- |
| LibreChat | Set `OMICSBASE_LIBRECHAT_IMAGE` back, move the `librechat/` checkout back to the old commit, and recreate `api`. |
| A config file | Restore the backup, then recreate `api` or reload Caddy. |
| The Caddyfile | Restore the backup and run `sudo systemctl reload caddy`. |
| The router | Restore the backup and run `sudo systemctl restart roihu-router`. |
| The engine on LUMI-K | Set the previous image in `engine.yaml` and apply it, or switch notes to the VM engine (see [Switch notes between LUMI-K and the VM](#engine-switch)). |
| The Reports image | Set `ROIHU_IMAGE_TAG` back and recreate `api`. |

After any change or rollback, check:

1. You can sign in.
2. A note runs an R cell and shows its plot.
3. The `notethreads` tools appear in the LibreChat log.
4. A public note opens without signing in.
5. Reports opens.
